verses.text: Hezekiah sent word throughout Israel and Judah, and wrote letters to Ephraim and Manasseh, inviting everyone to come to the LORD's house in Jerusalem to celebrate Passover to the LORD, the God of Israel.
The king, his officials, and the whole assembly in Jerusalem had agreed to celebrate Passover in the second month.
They couldn't celebrate it at the usual time because too few priests had consecrated themselves and the people hadn't gathered in Jerusalem.
The king and the whole assembly agreed that the new date was right.
They issued a decree throughout Israel, from Beersheba to Dan, inviting the people to Jerusalem to celebrate Passover to the LORD, the God of Israel. Few people had been observing it as prescribed.

At the king's order couriers went throughout Israel and Judah with letters from him and his officials. The letters said, "People of Israel, return to the LORD, the God of Abraham, Isaac, and Israel, so that he'll return to those of you who survived the kings of Assyria.
Don't follow the example of your ancestors and relatives. They were unfaithful to the LORD, the God of their ancestors, and he gave them over to devastation, as you can see.
Don't be stubborn like your ancestors. Yield to the LORD, come into the sanctuary he has set apart forever, and serve the LORD your God so his fierce anger turns away from you.

If you return to the LORD, your relatives and children will receive compassion from their captors and come back to this land. The LORD your God is gracious and merciful. He'll welcome you if you return to him."
The couriers went from town to town through Ephraim and Manasseh as far as Zebulun, but people laughed at them and mocked them.
Still, some people from Asher, Manasseh, and Zebulun humbled themselves and went to Jerusalem.
God also united the people of Judah so they obeyed what the king and officials had commanded in keeping with the LORD's word.
A huge crowd gathered in Jerusalem in the second month to celebrate the Festival of Unleavened Bread.
They took down the altars in Jerusalem, including all the incense altars, and threw them into the Kidron Brook.
They slaughtered the Passover lambs on the fourteenth day of the second month. The priests and Levites were ashamed, so they consecrated themselves and brought burnt offerings into the LORD's house.
They took their assigned places according to the law of Moses, the man of God. The priests received the blood from the Levites and sprinkled it.
Many in the assembly hadn't consecrated themselves. The Levites slaughtered the Passover lambs on behalf of everyone who was unclean, to dedicate the offerings to the LORD.

Many people from Ephraim, Manasseh, Issachar, and Zebulun hadn't purified themselves, yet they ate the Passover meal contrary to what was written. Hezekiah had prayed for them, saying, "May the good LORD forgive everyone
who sets their heart on seeking God, the LORD, the God of their ancestors, even if they haven't met the sanctuary's requirements for being clean."
The LORD heard Hezekiah and healed the people.

The Israelites who had come to Jerusalem celebrated the Festival of Unleavened Bread for seven days with great joy. Every day the Levites and priests praised the LORD with singing and loud instruments.

Hezekiah encouraged all the Levites who showed skill in serving the LORD. The people ate throughout the seven-day festival, presented peace offerings, and made confession to the LORD, the God of their ancestors.
The whole assembly agreed to celebrate for seven more days, and they did so with joy.

King Hezekiah of Judah gave the assembly a thousand bulls and seven thousand sheep for offerings. The officials gave a thousand bulls and ten thousand sheep. A great many priests consecrated themselves.
Everyone from Judah celebrated, together with the priests and Levites, the people who had come from Israel, and the foreigners who had come from Israel or were living in Judah.
Jerusalem was filled with joy. Nothing like it had happened there since the days of Solomon son of David, king of Israel.
Then the Levitical priests stood up and blessed the people. God heard them, and their prayer reached his holy dwelling in heaven.
